# Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes – Summary
The Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes is Germany’s largest and oldest scholarship foundation, originally founded in Dresden in 1925, dissolved during National Socialism, and re-established in Cologne in 1948. It supports exceptionally talented students and doctoral candidates, selected based on excellence, initiative, and responsibility, through a rigorous multi-channel admissions process. Applicants may be nominated by schools, professors, competition authorities, cooperation partners, alumni, or can self-apply via an assessment test; artists and musicians are admitted via university nominations. Scholarships are available regardless of citizenship, age, or field of study, provided the candidate attends a university in Germany, the EU, or Switzerland. Admission rates vary by nomination method, and further funding beyond the standard duration is contingent on academic progress and engagement.
The Studienstiftung provides both financial and academic support to undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral students—monthly allowances, need-based grants up to €855 (students) or €1,550 (PhD candidates, rising to €1,650 in October 2025), plus insurance subsidies and special funds for scholars with children. Academic support includes summer academies, research groups, language courses, workshops, and mentoring by liaison professors. Additional open and internal scholarship programs involve collaborations with external institutions (e.g., KAUST, McCloy, ERP, Carlo-Schmid, Max Weber program for Bavaria). As of 2023, the Studienstiftung funded 2,179 scholarships and 301 doctoral scholarships, with women making up more than half the scholars. Historically, the share of Studienstiftung scholars among Germany’s university students has grown from about 0.4% to nearly 0.5% (ca. 14,900 scholars in 2023), with a higher concentration at universities such as Bucerius Law School and Heidelberg University. Numerous distinguished alumni, including Nobel laureates, leading academics, businesspeople, politicians, artists, and journalists, testify to the foundation’s position as the country’s most prestigious academic scholarship provider.
